title: A typed title passes and an untyped one is refused with its reason, by --title, a message file and the commit-msg hook on main, while a branch's commits stay free-form
when: Checks typed, untyped and wrongly typed titles, by --title and a message file, then in a temporary git repo with the hook enabled commits on main, on a branch, and a squash merge of the branch into main.
then: Expects typed titles to pass and every other title refused with its reason; on main the hook refuses an untyped commit and the untyped squash and takes the typed squash, and on the branch it takes a free-form commit.

title: Nothing the Reader is looking at jumps
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: Open a page; move between records by the nav, a link, the graph, Back and quick find; collapse and resize the wiki card and the panels, fold rows, move around the graph and the ERD; reload while scrolled; open a tooltip and the overlays; switch the theme; and on a phone open and close the sheets.
then: Nothing on screen moves unless the Reader moved it: the nav, the page bar and the header strip stay put, the reload comes back at the same scroll, and the tooltip, overlays and sheets open where they show without pushing the page.

title: Move around a record with nothing jumping
when: Follows a link and goes Back. Opens the Graph pane and uses Expand all. Zooms the graph, and resizes the panes by dragging. Changes the record through the CLI while the page is open. Opens and closes quick find, and switches the theme.
then: Expects each move to stay within the layout-shift budget with its frame holding still. The performance budgets are judged by the performance suites.

title: Performance: big maps pan and zoom at 60 Hz, frame a walked focus within 200 ms, and lay out off the main thread, through a reload
when: On the production build over the large product, pans and zooms the Graph, the ERD and the Trace, walks the Graph's focus with the arrow keys, and pans the Graph while a CLI write changes a use case's title.
then: Expects no frame over 20 ms while panning and zooming each stage and through the reload, each walked focus framed within 200 ms, and the Graph's map laid out in the layout's worker within 4 s.

title: The Reader reads and moves around Lathe on a phone
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: On a phone, open Lathe, search for a use case by its ID, switch to the Graph, pinch and open a node, use the wiki card sheet, the nav sheet and the Open pages sheet; then use a tablet in landscape.
then: Text is readable without zooming, every target is large enough for a finger, no page scrolls sideways, the search opens the use case, the graph pans and pinches and opens the node, and each sheet opens and closes; on the tablet the panels show side by side.

title: Read the spec on a phone
when: At 375 by 812 with touch, opens quick find from the top bar and taps a use case. Taps Graph in the page bar and pinches out: the camera zooms in. Taps a node, which opens it. Swipes the wiki card sheet to full height, then away. Opens the nav sheet and chooses the domain; Back, twice, takes them back to the use case. At tablet landscape size: the workbench, with targets at least 40 px tall.
then: Expects each touch to do what it does on a phone, and the workbench on a tablet.

title: The Reader uses Lathe by keyboard and screen reader
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: With a screen reader on and only the keyboard, tab round the nav, the tab panel, the wiki card and the stage, open records, switch stages and collapse the wiki card, pick High contrast in light and dark, and open a dialog and a phone sheet.
then: Every control is reached by Tab in order with a visible focus ring and announced by its name and state, records open and stages switch from the keyboard, High contrast passes in light and dark, and focus moves into the dialog and the sheet and returns when they close.

title: Use Lathe with a keyboard and a screen reader
when: Tabs round: the nav, the page bar, the stage and the wiki card are reached. Opens a record by quick find: focus is not dropped. Opens Graph and collapses the wiki card: the announcer names each change. Picks High contrast by keyboard. Opens the palette: Tab stays inside; Escape gives focus back to its opener.
then: Expects every region reached, each change announced and focus held and returned.

title: The Reader works the whole app from the keyboard
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: In the app, with a screen reader on, press Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P and run commands from the palette and by their VS Code keys, Cmd/Ctrl+B among them; type in a search box; press ? and change a shortcut's key in the sheet.
then: Every command runs from its key and from the palette, the screen reader announces what changed, typing in a search box never fires a single-key shortcut, and the new key runs its command at once and after a reload, and shows in the shortcuts sheet.

title: Work the app from the keyboard
when: Opens the palette with Ctrl+Shift+P and finds a command with its keys. Hides and shows the navigation with Ctrl+B; the announcer speaks. Types g, t and ? in a filter box: they type and open nothing. Presses ?: the shortcuts sheet by group, with its search and a key to add to each shortcut.
then: Expects each command run by its keys and no shortcut firing while typing.

title: The Reader learns a shortcut where it is used
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: Rest on a control that has a shortcut, open the palette and the shortcuts sheet, and reach the control with a screen reader; then change its key in the sheet and look again.
then: The tooltip, the palette, the shortcuts sheet and the screen reader (`aria-keyshortcuts`) each give the same keys, and after the change each gives the new keys.

title: See each command's shortcut where it is used
when: Rests on the Graph button: its tooltip names its keys, which aria-keyshortcuts also carries. Reads a command's keys in the palette. Changes the navigation's Ctrl+B to Ctrl+J in the shortcuts sheet. Reads Ctrl+J in the tooltip and aria-keyshortcuts at once and after a reload, then in the palette, and runs it.
then: Expects every hint to follow the rebinding, and the new key to run the command.

title: The Reader works under Lathe's own title bar
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: In the desktop app, go back and forward from the title bar, click the command center, show and hide the navigation, drag the bar and double-click it, then change the theme.
then: Back and forward move through the history, the command center opens quick find, the navigation hides and shows, dragging the bar moves the window and a double-click zooms it, and the bar follows the new theme with no flash.

title: The title bar in a real window
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the window's own controls and the system's gestures, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/chrome.ts` or `app/src/shell/DesktopTitleBar.tsx`.
when: Run `npm --prefix desktop start`. The window has no system title bar; the traffic lights sit centered in Lathe's bar, clear of the back button. Drag the bar between its controls: the window moves. Double-click it there: the window zooms (or minimizes, if the system's setting says so). Click each control: it acts and the window does not move. Narrow the window: the command center shortens with an ellipsis and stays centered on the window. Choose another theme and switch between light and dark: the bar and the window's background follow, with no flash.
then: It passes when every step behaves as written.

title: The menus run the page's commands
manual_reason: Only macOS shows the native menu bar: a person checks it in the built app.
when: Open the menu bar in the desktop app and choose View items that stand for the app's commands.
then: The menus are File, Edit, View, Window and Help, and each View item does what its key does in the page.

title: The page in the desktop app finds window.latheDesktop, so it knows it runs there
when: Runs the real shell, hidden, on a small product folder and reads `window.latheDesktop.isDesktop` in the page.
then: Expects `window.latheDesktop.isDesktop` to be true.

title: The native menus, and a View item run by its command ID
when: Runs the real desktop shell, hidden, on a small product. Reads the application menu's top-level labels and the View menu's items. Sends View, Show or Hide Navigation by its command ID. Reads window.latheDesktop.isDesktop.
then: Expects File, Edit, View, Window and Help after the app menu, the View items, the navigation folded and the page knowing it runs in the desktop app. macOS only, as the whole smoke run.

title: A second launch or a folder opened from Finder goes to the running app
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: With the packed app running, runs `open -a Lathe ~/some/product` or drags a product folder onto the Dock icon, then does it again.
then: The running app opens the folder in a window, and the second time brings that window forward; no second app starts.
notes: T124 routes a second launch at unit level.

title: The window has no spell check, overlay scroll bars and native context menus, and reopens in full screen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: In the desktop app, scrolls a long page, right-clicks in quick find, then enters full screen, quits and reopens.
then: The scroll bars float over the page, the right-click offers Cut, Copy and Paste, and the window comes back in full screen with the title bar's back button at the left edge.

title: A killed run leaves macOS no window state to offer to reopen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: Force quits Lathe while it opens its window, then opens it again.
then: macOS does not offer to reopen windows; Lathe opens its own last folder.
notes: T127 (`desktop/test/persistence.test.ts`) checks the defaults at unit level.

title: The shell opts out of macOS window restoration, on a Mac and for a test harness's Electron
when: Starts the shell on macOS, elsewhere, and as a test harness runs the unpacked Electron.
then: Expects ApplePersistenceIgnoreState and NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows set on macOS and for the harness, and nothing elsewhere.

title: The Dock, the app menu and the error page behave as a Mac app's
manual_reason: Only macOS shows the Dock and the app menu: a person checks them in the built app.
when: Keep Lathe in the Dock with a folder that has check errors and one the engine cannot load; open the Dock menu, About Lathe and Settings…
then: The icon reads at every size, the badge counts the front window's errors, the Dock menu opens a folder and lists the recent ones, About shows the versions, Settings… opens Appearance, and the folder that cannot load opens the error page saying why.

title: A native Mac app at the screen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: Run `npm --prefix desktop run dev`: the Dock shows the icon with a DEV band. Run `npm --prefix desktop run pack` and open the app from `desktop/release/`: the icon is crisp in the Dock, in Finder's list view (16 px) and in Cmd+Tab, in light and in dark appearance. Open a folder whose checks report errors: the Dock badge shows their number. Fix one: the badge follows. Bring a window with no errors forward: the badge clears. Right-click the Dock icon: New Window opens the folder picker, and the recent folders are listed (packed app). Choose Lathe › About Lathe: a small window shows the versions; Source Code and Reference open in the browser. Press Cmd+,: the focused window shows Settings. On a record, click Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID in its facts, and right-click a record row, a graph node and the page title: the native menu offers the same three and each works. With the app running, run `open -a Lathe ~/some/product` (packed app) or drag a product folder onto the Dock icon: the running app opens it, and a second time brings its window forward. Open a new folder: the window shows the shell color and "Opening <product>…" at once, never white. Break a row of one of its data files and reopen the folder: the error page shows the message; fix it and click Retry. Scroll a long page: the scroll bars float over it. Right-click in quick find: Cut, Copy and Paste. Enter full screen, quit and reopen: the window comes back in full screen, and the title bar's back button sits at the left edge. Force quit Lathe while it opens its window, then open it again: macOS does not ask to reopen windows.
then: It passes when every step behaves as written.
notes: The nav keeps the theme's own color: the system's sidebar material was left out, since it needs a transparent window and nav, which would replace every theme's nav color with the system's gray and give up the shell color that keeps a new window from flashing.

title: Every stage, view and kind of record page measures clean on four phones
when: Opens every stage, every view over the stage and one record of each kind, its page in the wiki card's sheet, at 375 × 812, 390 × 844, 430 × 932 and 812 × 375 with touch, waits for each page's own signals that it is ready (fonts loaded, nothing busy, animations finished, every box still over three looks), and measures it with the five phone checks.
then: Expects no page wider than the screen, no text cut off without an ellipsis and its whole text as a name, no target under 44 × 44 px outside a sentence, no two targets over each other or one under a fixed bar, and no target scrolling cannot reach.
notes: Run with npm --prefix app run test:mobile, and in the browser batch (scripts/ci.sh --browser); each finding names its element, its phone and a cropped screenshot, gathered in app/mobile/results/.

title: Each phone check finds the broken element on a fixture page and passes the sound one
when: On fixture pages at 375 × 812 with touch, measures a page with content past the screen's edge, cut-off text, small targets, small targets with a hit box stretched past them (wide enough, too short, and one a neighbor covers), overlapping targets and a fixed bar, and targets clipped away, beside sound ones of each.
then: Expects each check to report exactly the broken elements, and none inside a pannable map.
notes: Run with npm --prefix app run test:mobile-measure: fixture pages only, no server.

title: An aggregate with more entities than the limit is a warning naming it, the count and the limit
when: An aggregate has more entities than max_entities_per_aggregate.
then: aggregate-too-large names it, its count and the limit.

title: A capability starting with The or an -ing word, naming an interface or holding a list is a warning; a noun phrase or a single -ing noun is not
when: Capabilities titled Invoice management, Billing, The catalog, Writing invoices, Web app, Tools, members and loans, and String lending are added.
then: title-breaks-convention warns of The catalog, Writing invoices, Web app and the list, each naming the rule broken, and of none of the others.

title: A use case naming one of its product's interfaces or an interface word is a warning; one goal of verb and object, or a list, is not
when: Use cases are added that name the command line, the product's Member portal, a page and APIs, that hold a list with a comma, and that join objects with and, refund a fee or grant capital approval.
then: title-breaks-convention warns of each that names an interface word, an interface word inside a longer word (capital) not included, and of none of the others: a use case's list is use-case-title-joins-goals's.

title: A use case titled with a CRUD verb over a record or data is a warning
when: Adds use cases titled Change a product's data, Edit a record, Update the data and Change Lathe's schema with a migration.
then: Expects title-breaks-convention to warn of the first three, each naming the CRUD verb, and not of the last, whose verb is not over a record or data.

title: A journey naming an interface, holding a list or titled with a CRUD verb over a record is a warning, as a use case
when: Loads the complete product with its journey and four more journeys: one naming the web app, one a list, one a CRUD verb over data, and one goal verb first.
then: Expects a title-breaks-convention warning on each of the first three, saying how a journey is named, and none on the fourth.

title: A title another record of its kind and product has, or one ending with a period, is refused
when: An aggregate titled " loan " is added beside the aggregate Loan, and an invariant is titled with a period at its end.
then: title-unique refuses both aggregates, naming the other; the entity Loan beside the aggregate Loan loads; title-period refuses the invariant.

title: Two rules of one function in one file load, and two rules of one name in two files are refused
when: A second invariant gets a rule titled as the first invariant's rule, in the same file, then in another file.
then: The data with one file loads and counts both invariants as built; title-unique refuses both rules of the data with two files, naming the other.

title: Every name in Lathe and the Tool Library is one to four words with no article first
when: Reads the titles of every name kind in Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library's.
then: None is longer than four words or starts with A, An or The.

title: A domain whose title or code names a technology layer is a domain-named-for-technology warning
when: Adds domains titled Web app, Records (code `DB`), Shop (described as served by its own server) and Guided tours.
then: Expects `domain-named-for-technology` warnings for Web app and for Records, whose code `DB` gives `its code DB says "db"`, and none for Shop, only described as served by its own server, or Guided tours.

title: A query not starting with Get, List or Find is a warning
when: Queries titled Get a loan, find a tool by name, Show overdue loans and Getaway tools are added.
then: query-title-verb warns of Show overdue loans and Getaway tools only.

title: A flow not titled by its use case, in or through, and its interface is a warning
when: A flow is titled in the pattern in several letter cases, then Borrow at the desk; then its use case is renamed.
then: flow-title-off-pattern passes each title in the pattern, warns of Borrow at the desk with the title to give it, and warns again once the use case is renamed.

title: Every policy in Lathe and the Tool Library reads When an event, then its reaction
when: Reads every policy's title in Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library's.
then: Each starts with When, its event, a comma and its reaction.

title: An event title with no past form as its last word or after its first is an event-tense warning
when: Adds events titled Return tool, Loan became overdue, Fee needed and Speed.
then: Expects `event-tense` warnings for Return tool and Speed, and none for Loan became overdue or Fee needed.

title: A specification starting with A, An or The is a warning
when: Specifications titled The tool is free, an active member, Theme is set and Area is open are added.
then: specification-title-article warns of the first two only.

title: A test titled Tests that or Should is a warning, a result is not
when: Use case tests titled Tests that…, Should…, Test whether…, Tests run one at a time and a result are added.
then: test-title-not-a-result warns of the first three only.

title: A code-bound title with whitespace, or an endpoint not titled by its method and route, is refused
when: Titles a command handler `the loan opener` and a table `Loans by member`; titles an endpoint `Borrow a tool`; then adds a data model titled `loan` for TL-LEND-EN02 beside the data model `Loan`.
then: Expects `title-form` to refuse the handler and the table, the handler's message saying a command handler is titled by one identifier exactly as in code, with no whitespace; the endpoint refused by a `check`; and the data model `loan` to load, since code compares exactly.

title: Each rule record is a rule of its rules.ts by the name its refusal carries, and each rule there has its record
when: Reads Lathe's rule records and every rules.ts under lathe/src, with the rule names their refusals carry.
then: Expects each rule record to name a rules.ts that writes a rule of its title, and each rule a rules.ts writes to have a record of that title naming that file.

title: Every kind has at most one lead text, required, and every test a required When and Then and no Given
when: Reads the schema of Lathe's own spec: every kind, part and declaration table's columns and CHECKs.
then: Expects no table with two of statement, goal, meaning and description, every one of them NOT NULL with its trim CHECK, the ten tests with When and Then required and no Given, and no description on the data model, value type, predicate, event type, service, table, flow and flow step.

title: A product kind with an optional lead text, or two, is refused
when: Declares a description field on the fixture's CLI command kind that is not required, then a required description and a statement, then one required description.
then: Expects the first refused as a lead that must be required and the second as a second lead after description, both `product-kind`; the third loads.

title: No query handler or projection imports a repository or an aggregate's model, and a handler reads only through its reader
when: Reads the imports and code of each converted slice's queries.ts, read-model.ts and reader.ts, every file that imports a reader, and the reader records.
then: Expects none of them to import a repository.ts or the aggregate's model type or row builder from its model.ts; each query handler to be given its reader by the runner and to take only types from its read model; the reader not to read source rows; a reader imported only by its own slice's queries.ts; and each read model to have one reader record naming that reader.ts.

title: A meaning that uses another term's title without a builds_on link is a warning
when: Terms use other terms' titles in their meanings: whole and plural, inside a longer term's title, inside another word, in backticks, and one already linked with builds_on.
then: term-used-unlinked warns only of the whole and plural uses with no link, naming the term used.

title: A domain's glossary lists each term after every term it builds on, otherwise by title
when: Terms are added with builds_on links, one through a term of another domain, and the domain is read with get-domain.
then: Its terms come bottom-up, ties by title, each with the terms it builds on.

title: The wiki and the nav list a domain's terms after the terms they build on, otherwise by title
when: Terms are added to a domain, one building on another listed after it by title, and the domain's folders are read.
then: The term folder lists them bottom-up: Basket, Mango, Zebra, then Apple, which builds on Zebra.

title: An aggregate, read model or obligation no outcome reaches is a serves-no-outcome warning
when: Loads the complete product, then the same with no capability serving an outcome.
then: Expects no warning, then a serves-no-outcome warning for each aggregate, read model and obligation, saying to write the use case that needs it or remove it.

title: A business outcome whose target says no date is an outcome-target-undated warning
when: Loads the complete product with its outcome's target given with no date, then with a year and with a span from an event.
then: Expects one outcome-target-undated warning naming the outcome, then none.

title: Only a composition nests; every other parent is a link
when: Asks the composition rule about each composed pair and a set of parent pairs that are links.
then: Expects each composed pair, tests included, to nest, and none of the others.

title: In the Map every record sits in an area or inside the record it is part of, once
when: Lays out the test product's Map and the grouped workspace's.
then: Expects every record once, every record inside a record to be its parent's composition, and every composed child inside its parent.

title: A use case whose actors' own steps change two aggregates is a warning; queries, refused paths and another actor's write are not counted
when: A member's use case is added whose steps open a loan and add a tool, and another whose steps also hold the librarian adding a tool, a query and a refused write.
then: use-case-changes-many-aggregates warns of the first, naming the Loan and Tool aggregates and the remedies, and not of the second.

title: Aggregates are counted per interface that offers the use case
when: A use case offered by two interfaces has a step of each interface's own changing a different aggregate, then one of them made every interface's.
then: use-case-changes-many-aggregates is silent while each interface's version changes one aggregate, and warns once a version changes two.

title: A use case titled with and, or or a list is a warning; parts named after with are not
when: Use cases titled Borrow and return a tool, Renew or return a loan, Read tools, members, loans, Borrow a tool with its case and charger, Return a tool and Borrow a sander are added.
then: use-case-title-joins-goals warns of the first three, naming the word or the list, and of none of the others.

title: A step in which a role that is not one of its use case's actors sends a command is a warning
when: A member's use case has steps in which the librarian adds a tool, a Librarian adds another after a clause, the librarian shows the free tools, and the member borrows a tool from the librarian.
then: another-actor-writes-in-a-step warns of the two writes by the librarian, and not of the query or the member's own step that names the librarian as its object.

title: Data that breaks the model is refused when it is written, across tables
when: With rows that break a key, a CHECK, a foreign key or a validation query (a step fulfilling another use case's requirement, a policy hearing two events, a field with two types, an ID outside its scope, a test with no file), loads or writes each through the store.
then: The store refuses each one then, naming its row and rule, and nothing is saved; no check is left to find it later.

title: A refused command leaves the data and the files as they were
when: A command that breaks the model is applied with others.
then: The whole write is refused and the data and its files stay as they were.

title: Every interface names one specific command: no two definitions share an ID, a CLI command, an MCP tool or a route, and every command of an aggregate with a slice has its definition
when: Reads every command and query definition, whose identities are generated from Lathe's records, and Lathe's command records.
then: Expects no ID, CLI command, MCP tool or route named by two definitions, and no command of an aggregate with a slice without its definition.

title: The one Button component draws every standalone action: ghost, primary, icon, with an icon, danger, and a link drawn as a button
when: Renders the Button as ghost, primary submit, icon, with the `plus` icon, danger, and as a link to `/DM`; reads the app stylesheet.
then: Expects each its element, type and classes (`button button-ghost`, `button button-primary`, `icon-button`, `button button-ghost button-danger`), a click handled, `buttonClass` giving the same classes, and the stylesheet to style them once: the ghost hover tint, the primary steel fill and a 44 px target on a coarse pointer.

title: Each app aggregate of Exploring and Platform is reached only through its repository, and its handlers, policies and rules are the records' one to one
when: Reads app/src's Exploring and Platform slices and their repository, handler, policy, rule and other code-bound records.
then: Expects only a slice's repository to touch its storage keys, one repository per slice with its load and save, commands importing only their own slice, every code-bound title declared in its file and every command and policy function recorded.

title: Each desktop aggregate is reached only through its repository, and its handlers, policies and channels are the records' one to one
when: Reads desktop/src and the repository, handler, policy, channel and other code-bound records.
then: Expects only repositories to touch the user data folder's files, one repository per slice with a load and a save, commands importing only their own slice, every code-bound title declared in its file, every command and policy function recorded, and every channel recorded once.

title: No kind, column, flag or check records an exception to a rule
when: Reads the schema's tables and columns, Lathe's check rows, the CLI's flags with every command's and query's fields, and the plugin's skills and the READMEs.
then: Expects no table or column that records an exception, a waiver or an opt-out, no check text that exempts, waives or excepts, no flag that skips a rule, and no doc that teaches one.

title: Changes are hard cutovers: no redirect, alias, legacy path or second signature is left
when: The app and the engine sources are scanned.
then: No redirect, alias, legacy path or second addressOf signature is found.

title: What serves no purpose is removed: no unused file, export or dependency
when: Runs knip on `app/`, `lathe/` and `desktop/`.
then: It finds no unused file, export, dependency or binary.

title: No command or icon outlives its purpose: every keymap command is handled and reachable, every named command is in the keymap, and every icon is drawn
when: Reads the app's source, its keymap and its icon table.
then: Expects no command unhandled or unreachable, no command named outside the keymap, and no icon drawn nowhere.

title: No style outlives its purpose: every class selector in the app stylesheets is used in app/src
when: Reads the app's stylesheets and source, and asks whether a class name nothing uses, and `graph-page`, are used.
then: Expects no unused class selector in the app's stylesheets, `a-class-nothing-names` reported unused and `graph-page` used.

title: Each kind is essential or accidental by kind, never by record: a test follows what it proves, a standard its type, an API requirement its product's interfaces
when: Loads the complete example product and reads its kinds, then takes away what provides its internal API's requirement, then makes that API public.
then: Expects each kind's complexity as its stage gives it (essential through interface design and for a test data set, accidental in the technical specification and for an endpoint, as-parent for tests and standard rules, by-type for a standard, by-interface for an API requirement, none only for an open question); the internal API's requirement is accidental and reported until provided, and essential on a public API.

title: An essential record that names technology its kind's group has no business with is a warning, by Lathe's words and the product's own
when: Gives a use case a goal that clicks, a UC requirement that names the Web app, a flow step that clicks and a flow its own interface, a view page buttons rows and JSON, a pattern rule HTTP and JSON, a view test a click, a domain a term Table and a use case that names it, a term Postgres; then gives another domain a term Column and a requirement of the first a column, with and without a database; then lists Postgres and Table among the product's technology words.
then: Expects accidental-in-essential to warn of the goal's and the step's click, the requirement's web app and the view's JSON only; the column, a term of another domain, not at all, the database still; and of Postgres and Table once the product lists them; the complete product draws none.

title: An essential record that names the shape of a technical record, a table written as storage, a file or folder, a route or a command line, is a warning; words that only sound technical are not
when: Gives the complete product a table entity_field kept in lathe/schema/ and an endpoint under /api/, then writes Lathe's own requirements from before their conversion (an entity's fields as its entity_field rows, an interface's POST /api/use-case/<command>, the merge driver's command line, the migrations in lathe/schema/) into its records, words that only sound technical into a use case, a route into an interface and a view; then adds a term entity_field.
then: Expects essential-restates-technical to warn of exactly the four records with the table, file, routes and command line they name, and the term to excuse the table.

title: The same requirement or step statement in three or more use cases or views is a pattern in disguise, read with the names of the aggregates and entities alike
when: Gives two use cases' requirements, one of them twice, the statement Lathe's views gave each aggregate's refused commands with the aggregate's name aside, then the catalog view's requirement the same with an an.
then: Expects no warning for two use cases, then essential-repeated to warn once, on the first record, naming all four records in three use cases or views.

title: An accidental record is a warning until a tooling record generates it, something provides it or a record above it, or it fills a slot serving an essential record
when: From the complete product, whose every accidental record is accounted for, writes a command handler, a UI component and two repositories by hand, takes away the providers of the data store and the generator and what the second repository persists, and fills the slot with the UI component, which builds a view requirement, the repository whose aggregate has a storage requirement and the repository that persists nothing; then takes away the engineering standard's provider and the record that meets its rule, and makes it a quality.
then: Expects accidental-not-accounted-for to warn of the command handler, the repository that persists nothing (it fills a slot but serves no essential record), the generator and the data store; then of the standard and its rule but never its test; then of nothing.

title: Each fill is listed as accidental debt in its domain, and the third fill of one slot makes it a pattern candidate
when: Reads the complete product, whose slot has two fills, then writes a third record by hand and fills the slot with it.
then: Expects the domain's coverage to list both fills as its debt with no pattern-candidate, then pattern-candidate to warn of the slot, naming its three fills.

title: An obligation something outside the product provides is built and proved through its provider
when: Takes away an invariant's rule, its fill and its test, then names the platform integration as the invariant's provider.
then: Expects the invariant neither built nor proved, then built and proved, its provider in its proof list and its chain's build.

title: The store refuses a fill of a record a tooling record generates: a fill is written by hand
when: Loads the complete product with its tooling record also generating a command handler that fills a slot.
then: Expects the store to refuse it with fill-is-hand-written, naming the record, the slot and the generator.

title: A fill serves the essential aggregate it persists, an essential record a product relation links it to in either direction, an outcome it measures, or an essential record under it
when: From the complete product, writes a repository by hand whose aggregate has no storage requirement and fills the slot with it; then adds an accidental product kind with an essential child kind, two product relations to an essential product kind (one each way) and one between two accidental records, and fills the slot with four records of the accidental kind: one linked to an essential record, one an essential record links to, one with an essential record under it, and one linked only to another fill; then has a business outcome measured by that last fill.
then: Expects accidental-not-accounted-for to warn of nothing while the repository persists its aggregate, and of the repository once it persists nothing; then of the fill linked only to another fill, and of no other; and of nothing once an outcome is measured by it.

title: An engineering standard and its rules fill no slot: a rule is accounted for when a record accounted for meets it, and the standard when one of its rules is
when: Takes away the engineering standard's provider, so only the fill that meets its rule accounts for it; then adds a second rule that nothing meets; then makes the record that meets the first rule written by hand and filling no slot.
then: Expects accidental-not-accounted-for to warn of neither the standard nor its rule; then of the second rule only, saying no record that is accounted for meets it; then of the command handler, both rules and the standard, the standard saying no record that is accounted for meets one of its rules.

title: A slot that says why its fills vary by design is no pattern candidate, and the reason is never empty
when: Reads the complete product with a third record written by hand filling its slot, once with the slot's reason that its fills vary by design, once without, and once with a blank reason.
then: Expects no pattern-candidate warning with the reason, one for the slot without it, and the blank reason refused on load.

title: No tracked file names a product Lathe was tried on, a person or a machine's path
when: Every text file `git ls-files` lists is scanned, case-insensitively and by whole word, for the name of a product Lathe was tried on for a client or a collaborator, a person's first name and absolute home or temp paths.
then: None is found outside the allow-list of the author fields, the package name and the repo URL's owner; each finding names its file and line.

title: Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library check clean and wholly proved on every merge into main
manual_reason: Run as the merge gate: before each merge into main, the coordinator runs `npm --prefix lathe run check` on the merged branch and refuses the merge on any error, warning or obligation short of designed, built and proved.
when: Runs `npm --prefix lathe run check` at the repo root on the branch about to merge into main.
then: Expects 0 errors, 0 warnings, and every coverage line at 100% designed, built and proved in both products.
